properties.description: Units of ada:pixelScaleX/Y, e.g. nm, um, mm. Normalise before comparing values.
CRS units per column step (world-file A).
CRS units per row step (world-file E). A world file conventionally makes this NEGATIVE to encode the y-axis flip; here the sense is carried by ada:originLocation, so this is a magnitude.
link to appropriate basemap image map
CRS x of the origin pixel (world-file C). Which pixel that is, is stated by ada:originLocation rather than assumed to be the upper-left.
CRS y of the origin pixel (world-file F).
CRS z of the origin pixel, where the registration is to a three-dimensional frame. A world file has no equivalent, and a planar thin section does not need one.
Whether coordinates are stage-defined or pixel-defined. If pixel-defined, are coordinates from stage, upperleftPixel, or centerPixel.
Units of the CRS coordinates, i.e. of originX/Y/Z. A world file carries no units.

The x-component of one ROW step (world-file B): how far CRS x moves per row, which is zero when the image axes are parallel to the sample axes. Non-zero whenever the stage was rotated relative to the sample frame -- the case a scale-and-origin model cannot express at all, which is why both off-diagonal terms are declared here rather than assumed away.

The y-component of one COLUMN step (world-file D): how far CRS y moves per column, zero for an axis-aligned image. Optional, and absent means zero, so a registration that omits both rotation terms is the axis-aligned case -- which is what every record carries today.
The location of the origin pixel of an image. Range: upperLeft, upperRight, lowerLeft, lowerRight, center

Link to an EXTERNAL world file that carries the affine transform, instead of stating the six parameters inline -- a .tfw beside a GeoTIFF, an ESRI .wld, or any sidecar of that form. Use it when the transform already exists as a file the instrument or the processing software wrote: restating those numbers by hand is a second copy that can disagree with the first, and the file is the authority.
A record states the transform ONE way or the other, which the anyOf below enforces: either the inline parameters (origin, scales, corner, coordinate definition) or this reference. Both together is permitted and is not recommended -- nothing can adjudicate a disagreement between them, and the inline copy is the one that goes stale.
READ THE DEPARTURES BELOW BEFORE TRUSTING A ROUND TRIP. A world file is not quite what this object says, so importing one into the inline terms, or writing one out from them, needs the sign and the unit handled deliberately rather than copied.
